content.title: About
content.content: Quinoa is the seed of the Chenopodium quinoa plant native to the Andes. The “fat added” version is pre‑toasted quinoa enriched with vegetable oils, which raises its energy density and gives a richer flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quinoa is a pseudocereal, not a true grain, but nutritionally it is often compared to rice and couscous.
The fat content is boosted to about 8 % by adding olive and sunflower oils.
Quinoa contains all nine essential amino acids, making it a complete plant protein source.
In ancient Andean cultures quinoa was called the “mother of all grains” and used in ceremonial dishes.
Toasting and adding fat shortens cooking time: the product is ready in 5‑7 minutes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: One serving (≈ 185 g) provides about 8 g of plant protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Added monounsaturated fats (olive oil) help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Quinoa supplies both soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Abundant micronutrients
items.content: It contains magnesium, iron, zinc, phosphorus and B‑vitamins, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Quinoa raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for diabetes management and weight control.

items.title: Pseudocereal allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to quinoa.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added fats increase the energy value to ≈ 210 kcal/100 g, so portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Quinoa contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fat‑added quinoa works well as a side dish, in salads, soups, or vegetarian patties. Rinse it first, then simmer in water (1 : 2 ratio) for 5‑7 minutes until tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated to prevent oxidation of the added oils.
